URI Faculty Senate Curriculum Toolkit
A shared resource for faculty and curriculum stakeholders navigating the University’s curriculum approval process.

passages.heading: What is the Curriculum Toolkit?
passages.text:
This toolkit helps faculty, committees, chairs, deans, and other stakeholders create, review, and advance curriculum proposals through the University’s approval process. It outlines roles, expectations, processes, and resources to support accurate, efficient proposals and effective shared governance.
The Playbook focuses on process, not content. Faculty remain the subject-matter experts on academic purpose, curriculum, and learning outcomes; this resource provides the framework for moving proposals smoothly through review and approval.
It is designed so that everyone can start where they need help without having to sort through guidance intended for other roles.

passages.heading: Choosing the Right Proposal Type
passages.text:
Choosing the Right Proposal Type
Course Proposal Types
There are two types of curricular proposals: modifying an existing curricular item or creating a new one. Selecting the correct proposal type is important. Proposals submitted under the wrong category will be denied and must be resubmitted.
Course modifications that are sometimes mistaken for new courses include:
Making a temporary course permanent
Changing the subject code of an existing course
Adding a new cross-listing to an existing course
A new course proposal is appropriate for:
Creating a new permanent course
Creating a new temporary course
Program Proposal Types
There are two types of curricular proposals: modifying an existing curricular item or creating a new one. It is important to select the correct proposal type, as proposals submitted under the wrong category will be denied and must be resubmitted.

passages.heading: Program Credential Types
passages.text:
In addition to selecting the appropriate proposal type, each program is classified under one of four credential types: Degree, Major, Certificate, or Minor. The credential type identifies the type of academic program being proposed.
Degree
An academic credential awarded by the University upon successful completion of a prescribed program of study. Degrees include bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral degrees.
In Kuali, select Degree when the program is the only program offered under that degree. Examples include the MPS (Master of Professional Studies), BIS (Bachelor of Interdisciplinary Studies), Pharm.D. (Doctor of Pharmacy), and DNP (Doctor of Nursing Practice).
Major
A defined field of study within a degree program consisting of a required set of courses and related academic requirements in a specific discipline.
In Kuali, select Major when the program is one of multiple options offered under the same degree. These typically include BA, BS, MA, MS, and PhD programs.
Certificate
A formal program of study consisting of a defined set of courses in a focused area. Certificates may be completed independently or in conjunction with a degree program.
Minor

passages.heading: Program Credential Types

A secondary field of study consisting of a prescribed set of courses in a discipline outside a student’s major. A minor is intended to complement a student’s primary area of study.
Specialization Proposal Types

passages.heading: 🚨 Understanding Specializations, Sub-Plans, Options, Tracks, Focus Areas, and Concentrations
passages.text:
At URI, these terms refer to different curricular structures. Understanding how they differ is essential to ensure that programs and their areas of study are proposed and documented correctly.
Specializations, Sub-Plans, Options, and Tracks
These represent a formally recognized area of study within a program. They:
Are coded in eCampus
Have defined requirements that students must complete
Appear on the student’s transcript
Are formally created and maintained through the Specializations section of Kuali
Note: The terminology used may vary by system or University Manual terminology. For curricular proposal purposes, these structures are treated as specializations in Kuali.
Concentrations and Focus Areas
These represent an optional area of study within a program. They:
Are not coded in eCampus
May include suggested courses or course sequences to guide students
Do not appear on the student’s transcript
Are described within the program description to which they belong
Do not require a separate curricular proposal

passages.heading: What about ABMs and “4 + 1” Programs?
passages.text:
Both Accelerated Bachelor’s to Master’s (ABM) programs and “4 + 1” programs are formally recognized Specializations, but they differ in how they are structured and which degree program they belong to.
ABM Specializations
Are inherited by the Master’s degree
Identify a defined pathway from the Bachelor’s degree into the Master’s degree
Include an identified set of courses that may be double-counted toward both the Bachelor’s and Master’s degree requirements
“4 + 1” Specializations
Are inherited by the Bachelor’s degree
Do not include courses that are double-counted toward both degrees
Provide guidance on courses students should take during the final semesters of their undergraduate degree to help shorten the time needed to complete the Master’s degree

passages.heading: Track Your Proposal
passages.text:
Track Your Proposal
Quick Links
Submitting a curricular proposal in Kuali begins a structured, multi-level review process, and we know you’re eager to know when your item will be reviewed and approved. While timelines vary across colleges, this guide will help you understand where your proposal is in the process and when to expect its full approval.

passages.heading: The Quick Version
passages.text:
For those who already know how the process works, but simply need directions on where to find the status:
Open the proposal in Kuali
Expand the workflow status

passages.heading: Step 1: Understand the approval path
passages.text:
All curricular proposals move through multiple levels of review. While this can vary slightly, most proposals follow this sequence:
Department-level review(s)
College Curriculum Committee
College Dean
Faculty Senate Curriculum Committees (Graduate Council, Curriculum & Standards, General Education)
Faculty Senate (courses are fully approved at this level)
University President (program modifications and new certificates, minors, and specializations are approved at this level)
Board of Trustees (new major and degree programs are approved at this level)
Each step depends on the successful approval at the previous level.
Check out ‣ for a flowchart and more detailed explanation of the approval process.

passages.heading: Step 2: Know the current proposal status
passages.text:
All who have access to Kuali have the ability to check on the status of every proposal currently under review. To find the current workflow status:
Open the proposal in Kuali.
Access it from your dashboard if you are the proposer, or
Search for it in the Proposals section, and use filters to refine results
Review the workflow status. At the top of the proposal page, the workflow status shows:
The current stage of approval
The users in the role of approving that step
Expand for full details. Clik the expand option to the right of “Workflow Status” to view:
The completed approval steps, and
The remaining steps before final approval.

passages.heading: Step 3: Know the submission deadlines
passages.text:
Department, college, and Faculty Senate committees each have deadlines for including proposals on their meeting agendas. Faculty should consult with their department or college curriculum committees for specific deadlines at those levels of approval.
Each summer, submission deadlines are set for college deans to help ensure proposals are approved by the Faculty Senate on a predictable timeline.

passages.heading: Step 4: Factor in Revisions
passages.text:
Many proposals require revisions during the review process. The following meeting results can impact your approval timeline:
Tabled: The committee needs additional information before making a decision. Once the requested information is provided, the proposal will be reviewed again at the next meeting.
Contingently Approved: The proposal is approved pending minor revisions or clarifications. No additional committee review is required. Once the conditions are met, the proposal will move to the next step.
Sent Back: The proposal requires substantial revisions. It must be updated and resubmitted, at which point it will re-enter the workflow from the beginning.

passages.heading: Step 5: Track Your Proposal Status
passages.text:
Proposal statuses can be tracked by logging into Kuali and expanding the workflow, or by searching for items that have been fully approved by the college in the proposal tracker.
‣
Please note: The proposal tracker is updated manually by the Faculty Senate Office and is not automated. While every effort is made to ensure accuracy, occasional errors may occur and are typically corrected after each Faculty Senate meeting. For the most up-to-date status, please check Kuali.

passages.heading: Step 6: Final Check
passages.text:
By the Monday prior to each monthly Faculty Senate meeting, the Faculty Senate Office distributes the Senate agenda to all faculty.
This agenda includes reports from the Graduate Council, Curriculum & Standards Committee, and General Education Committee, which are voted on during the meeting.
If your proposal has been approved by a committee but does not appear on the agenda, please contact the committee chair or the Faculty Senate Office. Reports are prepared manually, and with a high volume of proposals each month, occasional errors may occur. These are typically resolved quickly.

passages.heading: Course Proposals after the Senate Meeting
passages.text: The integration between Kuali and PeopleSoft is not immediate, can take several days, and requires review by Enrollment Services to ensure all information migrated accurately. Please allow up to two weeks after the Senate Meeting for new courses and course modifications to appear in eCampus.

passages.heading: Program Proposals after the Senate Meeting
passages.text:
Once curriculum committee reports are approved by the Faculty Senate, they are converted into Bills. Bills are signed by the Faculty Senate President and forwarded to the University President for review and signature. Once the University President signs & approves, the Bills are returned to the Faculty Senate Office and the proposals are approved in Kuali.
Special Case: New Majors and New Degree Programs
After University President approval, these proposals are forwarded to the Board of Trustees. Once the Faculty Senate Office confirms Board approval, the new major or degree is fully approved in Kuali.
The URI Board of Trustees meeting dates can be found here.

passages.heading: What is Kuali Curriculum Management?
passages.text:
Kuali Curriculum Management (CM) is URI’s system for managing university curriculum and the curriculum approval process. It uses electronic forms and workflow to route course, program, and specialization proposals through the appropriate levels of review and approval.
Kuali, the Catalog, and eCampus
Kuali serves as the central source for approved curriculum information:
Kuali CM — Manages curriculum proposals and the approval workflow.
Academic Catalog — Pulls approved course, program, and specialization information from Kuali.
eCampus — Receives approved course information from Kuali for implementation in future terms.
Why it matters
Information entered into Kuali can flow directly into the official academic catalog and eCampus. Proposals should therefore be clear, accurate, and unambiguous, as the information entered during the proposal process becomes part of the University’s official curriculum.

passages.heading: Access & Logging Into Kuali
passages.text:
Access to Kuali CM is limited to faculty, Deans, and select administrators and staff. Only faculty members may submit curriculum proposals.
Faculty Access
Faculty members automatically have access to Kuali CM, as faculty are the users authorized to submit curricular proposals. If this is your first time accessing Kuali CM, sign in using your URI Microsoft 365 account.
Non-Faculty Access
Access to Kuali CM is also available to deans and select administrators or staff. In specific cases, other non-faculty users may request access.
Use the Kuali Access Package to request access using your URI SSO. After selecting Continue, you will be asked to provide your job or position title and a business justification for needing access. Once your request has been reviewed, you will be notified whether access has been granted.
Logging In
Sign in to your Microsoft 365 Apps using your URI SSO.
Select Kuali Course Management from your application collection.
Alternatively, use the direct link to Kuali CM and bookmark it for future access.
Accessing the Curriculum App

passages.heading: Access & Logging Into Kuali
passages.text: Once logged in, select the Curriculum tile. This is where you can view current courses, programs, and specializations and, for authorized users, create proposals for new or modified curriculum.

passages.heading: The Kuali Dashboard
passages.text:
When you enter Curriculum Management, the Dashboard serves as your homepage. It provides quick access to your proposals and items requiring your action.
My Proposals
My Proposals allows you to:
Continue working on Drafts you have started but not yet submitted.
View submitted proposals and their current workflow status.
Access proposals directly from the Dashboard.
Any proposals you begin but have not yet submitted will appear as Drafts. From this section, you can continue editing or delete a draft.
Select View All to see your complete list of proposals. The list can be filtered, downloaded, and printed.
My Action List
My Action List displays your ten most recent items requiring action. These may include proposals that require you to:
Review and approve
Acknowledge
Edit and return to the workflow after being sent back by a reviewing committee

passages.heading: Navigating Kuali
passages.text:
Use the navigation bar on the left side of the screen to access courses, programs, specializations, and proposals, including drafts, proposals under review, and approved records.
🔎 Search and Filters
Use the search bar at the top of the Courses, Programs, Specializations, or Proposals pages to locate specific records. Use the filters on the right side of the page to narrow your results.
Status: Select Active when searching for current curricular items. Retired and Inactive statuses are not consistently used in Kuali CM.
Groups: Use Groups to locate curricular records associated with a specific department or college.

passages.heading: Versioning
passages.text:
Kuali uses colored bars to indicate which version of a curricular record you are viewing.
🟢 Current Version — The version currently in effect. For most records, the earliest version available in Kuali is Fall 2022, when URI began using Kuali. Earlier historical versions are available in eCampus.
⚪ Past Version — An earlier version of the record, including inactive records.
🟣 Future Version — A version scheduled to become active in a future term.
↕️ Use the arrows next to the term dates to expand the record history and select an earlier or future version.

passages.heading: Proposal Status
passages.text:
The status indicators below apply only when you are viewing a proposal and not the curricular record itself. The colored bar at the top of a proposal indicates where the proposal is in the curriculum approval workflow.
🟡 Draft — A new proposal or proposed change that has been created but not yet submitted to the workflow. Drafts can be edited or deleted.
🔵 Under Review — A proposal that has been submitted to the workflow and is currently moving through the approval process.
⚫ Denied — A proposal that has been denied during the review process. Denied proposals cannot be edited or resubmitted.
🟢 Approved — A proposal that has completed the required approval process and has been approved.
Tip: When viewing an approved proposal, you can switch to the current curricular record by selecting “View Active Course (Program / Specialization).”

passages.heading: The Approval Process
passages.text:
The curriculum approval process generally follows the sequence shown in the URI Curricular Approval Process Flowchart. Specific steps may vary by college, department, proposal type, and whether the proposal requires additional levels of review.
Overview
Proposal Development Faculty use the forms in Kuali Curriculum Management to develop the proposal and work with other stakeholders as appropriate.
Department Review The proposal is reviewed through the appropriate departmental process.
College Curriculum Committee Review The College Curriculum Committee reviews the proposal.
College Dean Approval The College Dean approves the proposal for Faculty Senate review.
Faculty Senate Curriculum Committee Review The Curriculum & Standards Committee, the General Education Committee, or the Graduate Council reviews the proposal.
Faculty Senate Approval The Faculty Senate considers the curriculum committee's recommendation and votes.
University President Approval Any curricular item that is not a course must be reviewed and approved by the University President.

passages.heading: New Specialization Proposal Walkthrough

New Specialization Proposal Walkthrough
This guide provides step-by-step procedural instructions for completing and submitting a New Specialization Proposal in Kuali. It focuses on navigating the form, including what to select or enter in each field.
*In Kuali, Specializations are also known as Sub-plans, Options, Tracks, and Concentrations.
The guide is organized by proposal section (panel), so you can jump directly to a section when you need help.
This guide does not provide guidance on course content or academic decisions. Consult your department and applicable curriculum committees for questions about developing the course itself.
Navigate by Section

passages.heading: Start the Proposal
passages.text:
From your browser, navigate to Kuali Curriculum Management (CM).
Select Curriculum to open your ‣ .
From the left-hand navigation menu, select Specializations.
On the Programs page, select + New Specialization in the upper-right corner.

passages.heading: Parent Program
passages.text: Inherit From Begin typing the name of the parent program, then select the program from the list.

passages.heading: Specialization Information
passages.text:
Effective Term & Year Select the term and year in which you intend the specialization to become effective. If the selected effective term has passed the applicable deadline by the time the proposal reaches the Faculty Senate, it will automatically be updated to the next available term.
First Graduation Term Select the term and year in which you anticipate the first students will graduate with this credential.
Level Select the level of the specialization: Undergraduate, Graduate, or Dual Dual applies to ABMs and 4+1 specializations.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Dual is chosen for Level.
Dual Type Refer to the linked pages above to understand the difference between ABMs & 4+1s
Academic Calendar Select the academic calendar for the specialization: Accelerated 7-week through URI Online, or Traditional 14-week with Summer and J-Term Sessions (must coincide with parent program).
Department Select the department in which the program is housed.

passages.heading: Specialization Information
passages.text:
Is this interdisciplinary? The intent of this question is to identify whether the parent program of this specialization is jointly owned by multiple academic departments. If yes, the percentage of ownership assigned to each department must be provided in the curriculum worksheet.
🔽 The following field will appear only if “Yes” is chosen for Is this interdisciplinary?
Additional Department(s) and College(s) Enter departments sharing ownership of this program.
Academic Specialization Title Enter the title of the specialization. See the linked page for title formatting guidelines.
Specialization Description List the requirements of the specialization. Only specialization-specific requirements should be listed here, and no program requirements should be duplicated.
Admission Requirements If the specialization has specific admission requirements, list them here. Otherwise, enter: “See admission requirements for {Program Title}.”
Total specialization credits (excluding program credits) Enter the number of credits required for this specialization.
🔽 The following field will appear only if ABM is chosen for Dual Type

passages.heading: Specialization Information
passages.text:
Total double-counted course credits Enter the number of credits double counted towards this ABM.
Attach Curriculum Worksheet
Upload a curriculum worksheet outlining the courses, credits, and other requirements that make up the proposed specialization’s curriculum within its parent program. You may use the University’s standard curriculum worksheets, or you may clearly include all requirements in a word document or PDF.

passages.heading: ABM Information
passages.text:

passages.text:
New Course Proposal Walkthrough
This guide provides step-by-step procedural instructions for completing and submitting a New Course Proposal in Kuali. It focuses on navigating the form, including what to select or enter in each field.
The guide is organized by proposal section (panel), so you can jump directly to a section when you need help.
This guide does not provide guidance on course content or academic decisions. Consult your department and applicable curriculum committees for questions about developing the course itself.
Navigate by Section

passages.heading: Understand URI’s Curricular Process
passages.text:
Familiarize yourself with URI’s curricular process before beginning your proposal. This will help you understand the steps involved in the curricular process and accurately estimate how long your proposal may take to reach approval.
‣
‣

passages.heading: Make Sure You Can Access Kuali CM
passages.text:
You will need access to Kuali Curriculum Management (Kuali CM) to propose any curricular item.
‣

passages.heading: Choose the Right Proposal Type
passages.text:
Some course proposal types can be easily confused. If you are unsure which type applies, review these common examples.
If you want to… | Use…
Make a Temporary Course a Permanent Course which appears in the Academic Catalog | Course Modification Proposal
Create a new cross-listing to accompany an existing course | Course Modification Proposal
Add a new topic to an open-ended topics course | New Course Proposal if the course is a GCH course No proposal needed for any other subject code. Contact Enrollment Services to add the new topic.
Add a new topic to a permanent topics course | Course Modification Proposal
Create a new 500-level section of a course to accompany the 400-level | New Course Proposal

passages.heading: Start the Proposal
passages.text:
From your browser, navigate to Kuali Curriculum Management (CM).
Select Curriculum to open your ‣ .
From the left-hand navigation menu, select Courses.
On the Courses page, select + New Course in the upper-right corner.
The following sections of this walkthrough are grouped by section of the proposal form.

passages.heading: Contact Information
passages.text:
Complete the following fields with your contact information.
Proposer Name Your name is automatically populated based on your Kuali account.
Proposer Title Enter your university role.
Proposer Email Enter your URI email address. This is the email reviewers will use if they have questions about your proposal.

passages.heading: Course Administration
passages.text:
Effective Term & Year Select the term and year in which you intend the course to become effective. If the effective term entered at proposal submission has missed the deadline by the time it reaches the Faculty Senate, this field will be automatically updated to the next available semester.
Academic Career Select the appropriate Academic Career from the available options. You may only choose one option. If you plan to offer this course in both the traditional and accelerated calendars, please provide a rationale in the Supporting Materials file upload gadget that comes after the description.
College Select the college in which the course is housed.
Department Select the department in which the course is housed.
Honors Program Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following field will appear only if “Yes” is chosen for Honors Program.
Honors Type Select HPR Course or H-section of Existing Course.
General Education Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following field will appear only if “No” is chosen for General Education.
Temporary Course Select Yes or No.

passages.heading: Course Information
passages.text:
Subject Code The subject code must be owned by the College and Department previously entered in the form.
Number A validation error will occur if you use a number already in use by the subject code. The course numbering system is found in UM 8.30.10.
Temporary course numbers end with an “X”
Grand Challenge course numbers end with a “G”
Is this a 400-level course available for graduate credit? Required for all courses. Select Yes or No, regardless of the course level.
Course Title
Abbreviated Course Title 29-characters max.
Course Description Course descriptions are written for students, not faculty, and must communicate clearly and concisely to them. Jargon, acronyms, and technical language should be avoided as much as possible. Anyone should be able to read the description and understand the nature and intent of the course.
URI course descriptions include additional course information such as credits, cross-listed courses, method of instruction, class hours, requisites, grading, graduate credit, and general education outcomes. Descriptions will be formatted to the catalog standard prior to final approval.

passages.heading: Course Information
passages.text: Supporting Materials Optional. Use this file upload to provide additional information that may be helpful to review committees before the proposal enters the approval workflow.

passages.heading: Modality, Method of Instruction, and Prerequisites
passages.text:
Modality Select all applicable options to indicate whether the course will be offered in person, online, or both. The specific modalities are provided for reference next to the checkboxes and are also defined in University Manual 8.30.30
Method of Instruction All courses must have at least one method of instruction. Note that “Online” is not a method of instruction; it was removed from the list of methods of instruction in 2025.
If the course has multiple methods of instruction, select the first as Primary and all additional methods as Secondary.
If the course has two or more methods of instruction, indicate how the methods are divided. This information is important for Enrollment Services; omitting it may delay final approval.
Requisites Can include prerequisites, corequisites, antirequisites, or other enrollment requirements.

passages.heading: Cross-listed Courses
passages.text:
Is this a cross-listed course? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following fields will appear only if “Yes” is chosen for Is this a cross-listed course?
Cross-listed course(s) for eCampus Click “Add New” to add all cross-listings.
Cross-listed course(s) for the Catalog Click the “+” and add all cross-listings again.
Cross-listed Department(s) Add all departments belonging to the cross-listed courses, even if one or more belong to the same department.
Letter(s) of support from cross-listed departments For new courses and course modifications, the “parent” department (the department associated with the course code on the proposal) must provide a letter of support from each cross-listed department.
What if my cross-listed course code belongs to the same department as the parent course code? For example, MCE and ISE are both in the Department of Mechanical, Industrial & Systems Engineering.
Just upload a document stating: “Both subject codes belong to the same department.”

passages.heading: Grading Method, Credits, and Repeat Criteria
passages.text:
Credits First, select whether the course has fixed credits or a credit range. Then enter the applicable credit amount(s) in the fields provided.
Grading Method Select letter grades, S/U, or both.
Can this course be repeated for credit? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following fields will appear only if “Yes” is chosen for Can this course be repeated for credit?
Maximum times course may be taken: Enter max number of times.
Maximum credits allowed: Enter the maximum number of credits a student may earn for the course. For example, a 3-credit course that may be taken three times for credit has a maximum of 9 credits.
Can students repeat within the same term? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following field will appear only if “Yes” is chosen for Can students repeat within the same term?
Maximum credits allowed per term: Enter the maximum number of credits a student may earn from this course within a single term.

passages.heading: New Course Considerations
passages.text:
Explain the purpose of the course. Enter a brief explanation of the course's purpose.
How is this course used within the curriculum? Select the appropriate option from the provided radio buttons.
🔽 The following field will appear only if if Core requirement… is chosen from How is this course used within the curriculum?
List all degree, major, minor, and certificate programs for which this course is required. List the name of all applicable programs for which the course is a required component.
By checking this box, I acknowledge that all courses must be approved via Faculty Senate vote before a program can be reviewed for final approval. Check the box to acknowledge that the course must receive Faculty Senate approval before a program requiring the course can receive final approval.
Content Overlap: Has the proposed course been discussed with any academic units that may have related or overlapping curricular interests? Select Yes or Not Applicable.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Yes is chosen from Has the proposed course been discussed with any academic units…?

passages.heading: New Course Considerations
passages.text: Supporting Documentation Provide documentation demonstrating consultation with departments that have related or potentially overlapping curricular interests.

passages.heading: Certification for New Courses by Originating Academic Unit
passages.text:
This section is completed by the Department Chair or, when applicable, the Director, Area Coordinator, or College Curriculum Committee Chair. Proposers should leave this section blank and proceed to the next section.
For those responsible for completing this section:
Certification by the Department Chair, Director, or Area Coordinator responsible for administering the course. Check the box to certify that the proposal has received the required approval by the faculty of the originating academic unit.
Name of Department Chairperson, Director, or Area Coordinator Enter your name.
Date of Faculty Vote Enter the date the faculty voted on the proposal.

passages.heading: General Education Outcomes
passages.text:
🔽 This section will appear only if Yes is chosen from General Education.
Learning Outcome 1 Select the appropriate learning outcome from the dropdown and complete the table for your first outcome.
Learning Outcome 2 Courses must have at least one General Education learning outcome and may have up to two. Based on your selection for Learning Outcome 1, the applicable options will be available in this dropdown. If you are not adding a second outcome, leave this field blank.
If selected, complete the table for your second outcome.
Is this a grand challenge? Select Yes or No.

passages.heading: Grand Challenge
passages.text:
🔽 This section will appear only if the course is for general education credit, and if Yes is chosen for Is this a grand challenge?
To qualify for the grand challenge overlay, complete the following questions.
GRAND CHALLENGE: Explain how the course title, syllabus, and assignments demonstrate the contemporary challenge addressed by the course.
INTERDISCIPLINARY: Explain how the course incorporates at least two disciplinary perspectives and provides opportunities for students to make interdisciplinary connections through assignments, activities, and/or experiences.
INTERDISCIPLINARY: Provide an abbreviated reading list organized by discipline that demonstrates the course’s disciplinary perspectives, and explain how each disciplinary perspective is integrated into major course assignments and activities.
ETHICS: Identify the ethical framework that allows students to weigh/evaluate issues. This topic needs to show up explicitly in the course schedule.
ETHICS: List the readings pertaining to ethics.
ETHICS: Describe how ethics is incorporated in some/all of the assignments and activities.

passages.heading: Library Impact Statement
passages.text:
Once the proposal is submitted to the workflow, it is automatically routed to the Library Subject Selector, who will complete and upload the Library Impact Statement. Other than completing the prompts in this section, no additional action is required from the proposer.
Supplementary resources you expect to use in proposed course Select all that apply.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Other is chosen from Supplementary resources...
If Other, please specify:
Will students conduct library research in this course? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following field will appear only if YES is chosen from Will students conduct library research...?
Please describe assignment(s) in detail.
LIST the critical journals, monographs, and electronic resources in the field that the University Library MUST have in order to support this course or program:
LIST any additional journals, monographs and electronic resources in the field that would support the course, but are NOT essential:
Library Impact Statement Document The Library Subject Selector will upload this to the proposal after the proposer submits to the workflow.

passages.heading: Submit to the Workflow
passages.text:
Once you have finalized your proposal draft:
Select Leave Edit Mode in the upper-right corner of the screen, just below the orange bar.
Select Submit for Approval to submit the proposal to the workflow.

passages.heading: So, what happens now?
passages.text: Your proposal will automatically be sent to the appropriate review committees. You may be contacted within Kuali Comments by the committees with questions to the proposal (an email will notify you automatically). You can also return to your proposal from your dashboard at any time to view the workflow status.

Important Information about Changing a Program’s Academic Calendar
If a program is currently offered on the Traditional Academic Calendar and you would like to move it to the Accelerated Academic Calendar, you cannot simply change the calendar while students are still enrolled in the program. The existing program must first be fully taught out. This requires a proposal to suspend admission to the program. Once there are no students remaining in the program, the program can be moved from one academic calendar to the other.

passages.heading: Course Modification Proposal

passages.heading: Background
passages.text:
Through RI General Law §16-32-10 , academic responsibility at URI is delegated to the President and the Faculty Senate. With the President’s concurrence, the Faculty Senate has the authority to formulate policy concerning teaching and research, study, exercise, discipline, and government.
The Faculty Senate has oversight of the University Manual, which contains the rules and regulations that govern faculty and students. Additional oversight functions include curriculum approval, which provides for the establishment, abolition, and merger of programs, departments, courses, and curriculum, including general education.
To facilitate its charge, the Faculty Senate is composed of a six-member Executive Committee, six standing committees, and special committees as needed. Once elected to serve a three-year term, Senators are assigned to a Standing Committee based upon their interests. Senators may also serve on joint committees of the Faculty Senate and the President.

passages.heading: URI Internal-Facing Survey Assistance (URI-IFSA)
passages.text:
The Faculty Senate recognizes that not everyone is trained in how to create and execute surveys. Nonetheless, even internal-facing surveys at URI should yield relevant and robust findings, and several URI faculty members have expertise in survey design/development. FSEC is creating a list of URI faculty trained in survey research who will volunteer to assist administrative and departmental offices, centers, institutes, unions, and other groups (henceforth referred to as survey organizers) to construct surveys as professional service to the university.
Where will the IFSA list reside?
The IFSA list will reside on the Faculty Senate website, which is openly accessible.
Who will manage the IFSA list?
Judy A. Van Wyk, Department of Sociology & Anthropology has agreed to construct/manage the IFSA list alongside the Faculty Senate Coordinator and apprise the FSEC Vice President about its status each January.
Who will be on the IFSA list?
The list will contain URI faculty members who volunteer to have their information posted on the list.
What will be on the IFSA list?

passages.heading: URI Internal-Facing Survey Assistance (URI-IFSA)
passages.text:
Every faculty member on the list must be willing to volunteer survey assistance. To volunteer, faculty will complete a short questionnaire .
Responses will be posted on the IFSA website.
Questions on the form include faculty name, contact information, areas of expertise in survey research, and their willingness to be contacted by other URI faculty for contracted or volunteered survey-related activities (which is not a requirement).
How will volunteers be selected to assist with surveys?
Survey organizers will access the IFSA list when assistance is needed, and they will select a faculty member from that list based on their areas of expertise they have listed in the questionnaire.
Survey organizers will contact faculty members directly via email or by phone. (If volunteers or survey organizers need assistance, contact Judy Van Wyk at vanwyk@uri.edu , or Lisa Bourbonnais at lbourbonnais@uri.edu .
Faculty are encouraged to respond to requests in a timely manner.
Do faculty members have to volunteer when they are contacted?
No. All faculty members are incredibly busy and may not be available when contacted.
What are volunteer tasks?

passages.heading: URI Internal-Facing Survey Assistance (URI-IFSA)
passages.text:
Specific tasks will be negotiated between faculty members and the survey organizers. The intention is to help/assist URI offices with professional survey development. Needs may vary, and the availability and expertise of faculty will vary.
Possible Examples
Faculty may meet with organizers before a survey is written to clarify the purpose and intent of the survey.
They may want to review survey drafts written by organizers and provide suggestions for revision, or they may wish to write the survey questions to be reviewed by the organizers.
Additional tasks may be negotiated and should be compensated by survey organizers.
Possible Examples
Faculty might input the survey for electronic administration in survey software or prepare paper formatting.
They may facilitate a focus group to test the survey instrument.
They may compile responses and create a database for the organizers.
They might analyze the data for the organizers and present their findings to them.

passages.heading: URI Internal-Facing Survey Assistance (URI-IFSA)
passages.text: Ethical guidelines : Survey organizers should be reassured, and faculty consultants should undertake, that work on a survey remains confidential and any discussions or draft language (even if not finally adopted) should never be shared, even after the survey period has passed.

passages.heading: Faculty Senate Executive Committee
passages.text:
Through RI General Law §16-32-10, academic responsibility at URI is delegated to the President and the Faculty Senate. The Faculty Senate Executive Committee (FSEC) serves as the steering committee of the Senate. It represents the Senate in meetings with other University bodies and with the Provost, the President, and the URI Board of Trustees. Meetings of the FSEC are held weekly to coordinate the Senate’s business and its committees and address concerns within its jurisdiction.
For the description of the powers and duties of the Executive Committee, please see University Manual Appendix C: By-laws of the Faculty Senate, Section 4.1 – 4.9.

passages.heading: Classroom Steering
passages.text: The Joint Classroom Steering Committee (JCSC) shall serve as a steering group to the functional areas that manage and have responsibility for classroom upkeep and planning (MTS, Enrollment Services, and Business Services). The committee shall be responsible for the development of plans for all aspects of classroom planning and management, including, but not limited to, the development and management of a single classroom data-base, the establishment and updating of design standards, scheduling and planning, assessment of needs for classroom refurbishments and setting priorities, maintenance and ongoing management of classrooms and the coordination of resources for classroom upkeep and improvement. This committee shall also monitor progress and the execution of these plans. This committee shall be comprised of representatives from enrollment services, instructional technology, space planning, business services, property, facilities, the university architect, the President, the Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs, and at least three representatives of the faculty, one of whom shall be an academic department chair, appointed by the Faculty Senate. The chairperson shall be selected by the committee and confirmed by the Faculty Senate and the President. (University Manual 5.85.10 )

passages.heading: Space Allocation Committee
passages.text: The Space Allocation Committee (SAC) shall consider the present and future space needs of the University community, including new projects falling below the State’s Capital Improvement Plan project threshold. The committee will provide recommendations regarding space allocations requested to meet the programmatic needs of the University’s colleges and divisions. In making its recommendations, SAC shall consider future priorities of the University with respect to space, take into account the University’s academic priorities and strategic initiatives, and communicate with the Division of Research and Economic Development, the Campus Master Plan Review Team (5.40.10-5.40-13), the Joint Classroom Steering Committee (5.85.10-5.85.12), and the Strategic Budget and Planning Council (5.55.10 – 5.55.14) as needed. The Vice President of Administration and Finance shall review and approve space allocation recommendations prior to implementation.

passages.text: The Committee for Research and Creative Activities (henceforth referred to as the “full committee”) shall consist of six faculty senators and five non-senator research-active faculty) and students active, experienced, or concerned with various aspects of research, creative, and scholarly efforts at URI. passages.text:
The full committee shall serve as the representative voice of the university community in all matters related to research, creative, and scholarly activities. It shall seek to improve the environment for research at URI in all ways possible. The Chair of the full committee shall serve as an ex-officio voting member of the Intellectual Property Committee (See University Manual section 5.30.10). passages.text: The Budget and Administration Committee (BAC) shall comprise five faculty members, three of whom shall be faculty senators.
